newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos' party mates, cabinet officials and key business supporters are behind a multi-pronged campaign to amend the Constitution in order to allow him to run for reelection, sources in Malacanang and the administration Lakas NUCD party said. (MANILA TIMES)

- The country's three oil refiners have asked for an increase of at least 13 centavos per litre in the prices of petroleum products to cover additional costs of production incurred since early this year. (MANILA TIMES)

- The government plans to sell $12 million worth of jewellery confiscated from the family of the late ousted President Ferdinand Marcos in an auction that will coincide with a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders in the Philippines next month. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Petron Corp is considering exporting its first gas oil cargo because of an expected surplus in domestic supplies and to take advantage of high international prices, a company source told Reuters in Singapore. (TODAY)

- The Manila International Futures Exchange will not be allowed to resume operations until after it has submitted specific rules to stop abuses in futures trades, Securities and Exchange Commission head Perfecto Yasay said. (MALAYA)

- Total domestic and export sales of the Solid Group, the newly listed holding company of Elena Lim and foreign partners, increased 77 percent during the first eight months of the year, information obtained from the company showed. (MALAYA)
